Outcome: Depression cases (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: benefit
Claim: Older adults with low serum 25OHD levels were more likely to have elevated depressive symptoms overall.
Sentence: "Overall, there was a significant association between low 25OHD levels and elevated depressive symptoms (odds ratio [OR] = 1.58, 95% confidence interval [CI] = 1.20-2.07 for the lowest quartile; OR = 1.45, 95% CI = 1.15-1.83 for <30 nmol/L cut-off and OR = 1.34, 95% CI = 1.10-1.62 for the ≤50 nmol/L cut-off) after adjustment for a wide range of covariates of clinical significance."
Measured as: elevated depressive symptoms (CES-D)
Population: Older adults from the English Longitudinal Study of Ageing
Intervention: Serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D level (observational, no intervention)
Comparator: Higher 25OHD levels
Design: cross-sectional study
Sample size: 5,607
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

## Study B
Found: harm
Claim: Vitamin D level was significantly related to risk of depression (PHQ-9 above 5) six months after COVID-19 hospital admission; the direction is not stated in the abstract.
Sentence: "The variables that were significantly related to the risk of depression 6 months after admission for COVID-19 were frailty (p = 0.006 for pre-frail and p = 0.001 for frail), small-vessel vascular disease in imaging tests (p = 0.033), vitamin D level (p = 0.006), and taking antidepressants (p = 0.011)."
Measured as: risk of depression (PHQ-9 above 5)
Population: 72 patients admitted to a hospital in Spain for COVID-19, assessed at discharge and six months later
Intervention: Serum vitamin D level (measured, not administered)
Comparator: Lower versus higher vitamin D levels across participants
Design: cohort study
Sample size: 72
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

{
  "rationale": "Both observational studies examine serum vitamin D levels and depression, differing primarily in their populations (community-dwelling older adults vs hospitalized COVID-19 survivors) as well as outcome instruments and study designs.",
  "verdict": "genuine",
  "reason": "population",
  "also_differs": ["outcome_measure", "design_or_bias"],
  "detail": "population: 5,607 community-dwelling older adults vs 72 patients six months after COVID-19 hospitalization (note: Study B's abstract only reports p = 0.006 without stating direction)"
}
